bullets.title: NVDA: First H200 AI GPU shipments confirmed to China, but volume described as 'trivial'
bullets.body: Multiple U.S. officials confirmed that NVIDIA H200 AI chip shipments to China have begun—roughly two months after the Trump-Xi meeting. The Commerce Department previously cleared ~10 Chinese entities; one source noted only a small initial batch cleared the licensing/inspection pipeline, and the volume remains 'very few' or 'trivial.' Large-scale H200 shipments have NOT resumed. NVDA also announced a data-center cooling/power partnership with Mitsubishi Heavy.

bullets.title: AAPL: KeyBanc cuts to Underweight; PrismML on-device AI talks in parallel
bullets.body: KeyBanc downgraded Apple to Underweight from Sector Weight, citing weaker device demand and slower U.S. services revenue growth; shares were down ~1% premarket on the cut. Separately, CNBC and others report Apple is in talks with PrismML, a startup that compresses AI models to run natively on iPhone, potentially reducing dependence on cloud inference.

bullets.title: UBER: Advanced talks to acquire Delivery Hero at significant premium (~$13B value)
bullets.body: Multiple reports confirm Uber is in advanced talks to take over German food-delivery company Delivery Hero, with UBER said to be planning a bid well above Delivery Hero's recent trading price; Delivery Hero is valued at just under $13B. UBER shares fell ~2.5% on the news as the market weighed dilution risk from a large international acquisition.

bullets.title: HUBS: Sales desk flags 10-15% revenue tracking below plan ahead of earnings
bullets.body: A Raymond James call-out on HubSpot characterized the setup as 'nasty,' with the company reportedly tracking 10-15% below its revenue plan. Enterprise SaaS names broadly (HUBS, NOW, TEAM) were noted as selling off in sympathy with IBM's earnings warning.

bullets.title: MU: Whale accumulates $16.3M in short-dated calls; position up ~40% overnight
bullets.body: A large options participant accumulated $16.3M in short-dated Micron calls less than an hour before the prior session's close; Micron gapped up overnight, with the position reportedly up +40% and generating an estimated $6.5M in profit. Separate analyst commentary flags lower inflation and rates as incrementally bullish for the memory/storage trade alongside the AI infrastructure cycle.

bullets.title: ORCL: Shares plunge to 1-year low, down ~30% over the past month
bullets.body: Oracle shares hit a 1-year low and are down roughly 30.5% over the past month. Separately, Oracle announced an AI-native builder experience for agentic applications integrated into Oracle Fusion Applications.

bullets.title: TSEM: Japanese government-backed 300mm SiPho/SiGe capacity expansion announced; CPO delay flagged
bullets.body: Tower Semiconductor announced a Japanese government-backed expansion of 300mm Silicon Photonics, Silicon Germanium, and advanced packaging capacity, targeting $1.2B in net profit. Separately, at least one trader flagged a CPO (customer product order) delay as a near-term headwind. MRVL and TSEM were also highlighted as a bullish pair in AI photonics by multiple commentators.

bullets.title: SMCI/AMD/NVDA: AI infrastructure buildout narrative intact; Helios, Vera Rubin, liquid cooling in focus
bullets.body: Supermicro CEO discussed next-gen AI server design including AMD Helios (already has public launch-partner customers not resisting double-wide racks), NVIDIA Vera Rubin, liquid cooling, and storage as the primary consideration. AMD Helios global supply chain is operational. The 2023-2025 infrastructure trade (NVDA, TSMC, memory) is seen shifting to a 2026 model-lab trade as Anthropic ARR surges from $9B to $44B+.

bullets.title: AMZN: Anthropic stake seen as materially undervalued in stock price
bullets.body: A market commentator argued that Anthropic's value is not reflected in Amazon's share price—noting a hypothetical $3T Anthropic IPO would represent ~20% of AMZN's current market cap, and that AWS at a 'normal' multiple plus the Anthropic stake could justify AMZN's entire valuation alone.

bullets.title: GOOGL: Commits to 100% offtake on 1.6GW Arkansas solar project starting 2029
bullets.body: Google signed an agreement to purchase 100% of the energy output from the Steel River Energy Center in Arkansas, a 1.6 gigawatt solar project described as the biggest of its kind to break ground in the U.S., with operations expected to begin in 2029.

bullets.title: META: Most bearish options flow of the day; AI layoff targeting lawsuit adds headline risk
bullets.body: META exhibited the most bearish options flow among tracked names today. Separately, Reuters and others reported a lawsuit alleging Meta used biased AI-powered software to target workers with medical conditions for mass layoffs, raising legal/reputational risk.

bullets.title: NBIS: $1B+ Reflection AI compute deal announced but stock falls 5%; sits 30% off highs
bullets.body: Nebius (NBIS) signed a $1B+ compute agreement with Reflection AI for GB300 access through 2029; Reflection AI also inked a multi-billion dollar deal with SpaceX. Despite the contract announcement, NBIS fell 5% on the news, suggesting the market is skeptical of near-term revenue conversion. Stock remains ~30% below recent highs.

bullets.title: AVGO: Industry contact says Broadcom revenue could double via MediaTek integration by decade end
bullets.body: A well-sourced commentator noted that industry conversations consistently reference Broadcom's revenue line growing substantially through the MediaTek acquisition, with MTK potentially doubling its current business by end of decade, and argued that margin concerns are overstated.

bullets.title: NFLX: Content library + algorithm cited as durable competitive moat in streaming wars
bullets.body: Per LightShed podcast, Netflix's combination of scale (large content library) and a strong recommendation algorithm creates a durable competitive advantage in the battle for time spent, with success determined by retention and content discovery capabilities.

bullets.title: NY data center moratorium: executive order, not law—JMP Citizens analyst expects it to ease
bullets.body: New York became the first state to impose a one-year moratorium on new data center construction, citing energy and environmental concerns. A JMP Citizens analyst noted the moratorium is via executive order (reversible) and that cost-benefit clarity will ease regulatory pressure; broader commentary suggests 25+ state-level moratoriums would be insufficient to meaningfully constrain U.S. data center capacity given available sites and tax incentives.

bullets.title: June CPI: Headline -0.4% MoM, YoY 3.5% (est. 3.8%)—biggest monthly drop since COVID
bullets.body: June CPI came in sharply below consensus: headline -0.4% MoM vs. -0.1% expected (first MoM decline since 2020), core 0.0% MoM vs. +0.2% expected. YoY headline fell to 3.5% from 4.2%; core to 2.6% from 2.9%. 3M annualized CPI dropped from 8.2% to 2.8%. Supercore services fell 0.2% MoM (pandemic-era low). Rate-hike odds collapsed to ~13-14%. Warsh nonetheless cautioned 'mission accomplished' is not his view and more work remains on inflation.

bullets.title: MU/SNDK/LITE/NVDA: AI memory complex flagged for potential 'epic shakedown' of data center operators
bullets.body: One analyst warned an 'epic shakedown' of data center operators is coming that will reverberate through memory and semiconductor suppliers (NVDA, MU, SNDK, LITE), framing the CRAVE thesis (Cost Reduction and Value Expansion in generative AI). Separately, lower inflation and rates were highlighted as incrementally positive for the memory/storage trade.
